subject: The Tempo tab of Logic's List Editors, as a tempo-map readback
question: Is there a readable tempo map, and does it follow what the product writes?

reverify.command: Manual because it switches a UI tab: (1) open the List Editors; (2) press the Tempo tab; (3) read the table's header titles and rows; (4) drive `logic_transport.set_tempo` and read the table again; (5) restore the tempo.
reverify.expected: The table's headers are Position / Tempo / SMPTE Position, and the tempo cell changes to the value just written.

method: The List Editors' Tempo tab was pressed through AX and the pane's tables were dumped. `logic_transport.set_tempo` was then driven to 132 and the table re-read, then the tempo was restored to 120.

observations.what: the tabs the List Editors pane exposes
observations.note: localised descriptions; the Event tab is the one the note readback already uses

observations.what: the Tempo tab's table at 120 BPM

conclusion: The tempo map IS readable, through the same List Editors pane the note readback already uses. Its table names its columns — Position, Tempo, SMPTE Position — and the tempo cell FOLLOWS a product write: `set_tempo` to 132 returned State A and the row read `132.0000` immediately after. ADR-016's first public step is read-only Smart Tempo state and tempo-map inspection, and the inspection half has a working surface today.
limits: One tempo event. This project has a single entry at bar 1, so nothing here exercises a VARIABLE tempo map — several rows, ordering, or a tempo change partway through a project — which is what the word `map` in this ADR is mostly about.
Reading is not Smart Tempo. Project tempo mode, per-region Flex & Follow, analysis jobs, beat and downbeat markers and locked ranges were not looked at, and none of them appears in this table.
The second table in the same pane reports sixteen rows whose cells read empty. What it is was not established, and it is not the tempo map.
Column titles are localised (`위치`, `템포`, `SMPTE 위치`). Anything built on this needs a label set, exactly as the Event List's headers do.
The write used here is the ordinary transport tempo. This record says nothing about whether a tempo-map MUTATION — inserting or moving a tempo event — is possible or verifiable.
